extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural applicants, principal investigators, and institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Peer review summary and criteria for an NIH G11 institutional research administration training application, using standard NIH review dimensions (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) plus administrative determinations and budget recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (Impact/Priority score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: reviewers' assessment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field or institutional capacity; the summary presents an overall impact narrative for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact/Priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by individual reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance — Does the application address an important problem or critical barrier to progress in the field? For this application, whether strengthening Makerere University's grants administration addresses an important institutional/regional need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: addresses an important problem; clearly outlines gaps to be addressed; detailed processes and work tools identified; facilitates strengthening at the grantee institution and in-country/regional institutions. Weaknesses noted: none identified in some critiques; other critiques noted that over 70% of administrative staff lack training (a contextual weakness) and potential program demand may outstrip capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) — Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited, experienced, and capable of carrying out the proposed work? Evaluation of PI track record and team composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: PI possesses 8+ years as a senior grants administrator, extensive mentoring/training experience, and requisite authority; U.S. consultant (GWU) has appropriate skills; assembled team covers relevant areas. Weaknesses: none identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation — Does the application employ novel concepts, approaches or methodologies? For this project, novelty in pedagogy and tools for research administration capacity-building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: novel pedagogy including a Research Administration Buddy Program and an Online Learning Café; leveraging a lunchtime Seminar Series and reusable regional webinars. Weaknesses: in some reviewers' view, training aspects are solid but not unusually innovative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach — Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the stated aims? Includes feasibility of training plans, specific aims, and implementation tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: overall strategy and methodology appropriate; sound training plans in-country and in the U.S.; well-delineated U.S. training program; three specific aims comprehensively address needs; Table 5 shows task cohesion. Weaknesses noted: few details about installing and integrating a new Grants Tracking system with financial systems; uncertainty about availability of enough senior administrators to serve as buddies; concerns whether the planned rate of SOP development/updates is realistic; significant activity expected for limited PI and staff effort percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment — Will the institutional support, facilities, and resources contribute to project success? Evaluates institutional commitment and collaborative resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: Makerere environment combined with GWU resources are excellent; governance structure (PAC and PIT) well-positioned for change management; institutional commitment and requested resources appropriate. Weaknesses: none broadly identified; some concern about assessing implementation demands of new grants tracking system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection of Human Subjects — Determination of applicability and compliance (here coded NOT APPLICABLE (CODE 10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document states: PROTECTION OF HUMAN SUBJECTS: NOT APPLICABLE (CODE 10). Include this determination in summary statements when no human subjects are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertebrate Animal Subjects — Determination of applicability and compliance (here coded NOT APPLICABLE (CODE 10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document states: VERTEBRATE ANIMAL: NOT APPLICABLE (CODE 10). Include this determination in summary statements when no live vertebrate animals are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources — Applicability and reporting (here listed as NOT APPLICABLE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document states: AUTHENTICATION OF KEY BIOLOGICAL AND/OR CHEMICAL RESOURCES: NOT APPLICABLE. When applicable, reviewers check for plans to authenticate key resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Institution Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign Institution — Justification for funding a foreign (non-U.S.) institution and whether justification is adequate (here: FOREIGN INSTITUTION: JUSTIFIED. Uganda).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an application is from a foreign institution, reviewers and staff evaluate and record whether the foreign institution is justified for the award mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary Overlap and Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgetary Overlap / Committee Budget Recommendations — Review and recommended modifications to the requested budget and identification of overlaps or inconsistencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary notes that the administrative budget shown is requested and may be adjusted by grants management staff. Committee recommended clarifications (e.g., differences between budget base salaries requested on different pages need clarification). Grants management staff will calculate final costs based on recommendations in the Committee Budget Recommendations section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Policy and Scoring Process Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy notes on NIH resubmission limits and the process by which scores are produced and used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH modified policy regarding receipt of resubmissions (amended applications) is referenced (NOT-OD-18-197). The impact/priority score calculation process is explained: average of overall scores (1-9) multiplied by 10; criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting and are not discussed or mathematically combined into the overall impact score during the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Performance Monitoring and Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Project performance monitoring & evaluation framework — presence and quality of mechanisms to monitor, evaluate, and adapt the project during implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: a good project performance monitoring and evaluation framework is in place, guided and overseen by a Project Advisory Committee (PAC) and Project Implementation Team (PIT). Reviewers regarded this as enhancing adaptability and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability and Capacity-Building / Post-award Continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustainability plan — plans for sustaining project activities after the award period, and building local capacity for continued operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: demonstrated sustainability plan (e.g., post-award in-house grants management career track with modest registration fees) and plans for cascading training (training senior admins who will train junior staff and regional administrators). Reuse of recorded webinars to expand impact was highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Plan Detail and Feasibility (numbers, modalities, partnerships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity, feasibility, and organization of the staff training plan, including in-country and US-based training, numbers to be trained, modalities (hands-on, webinars), and partner institution roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: clearly delineated training plan, realistic numbers (2 senior leaders, 69 junior administrators, 56 scientists, 25 regional admins), well-laid-out coursework, use of GWU and NIAID resources, and low-cost, reusable webinar approach. Weakness: few details about grants tracking system installation and integration; uncertainty about availability of senior administrators to mentor juniors.
